newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends slightly firmer in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends slightly firmer in quiet trade.

text.p: COMEX copper ended only slightly firmer Tuesday, with LME copper prices also steady for a third day in a row, after last week's volatility.

"There's very little volume or sense of direction at present," Triland USA trader Brent Tolen said. "Last week's rally ended as quickly as it began, and with some business still to be sorted out from the Sumitomo affair, many traders are only doing what they need to at present."
COMEX December copper ended up 0.15 cent at 90.00 cents, after trading in an 88.80-90.30 cent range.
Earlier LME copper found some support on a fall in LME warehouse stocks by 2,525 tonnes to 271,150 tonnes.
The December/March backwardation widened again to 1.80 cents, from 1.35 cents at Monday's close.

Both COMEX copper and LME copper prices have swung in a wide range in the past ten days, partly on options related trade as short positions, established during the Sumitomo affair earlier this year, were unwound.
"But business here in the U.S. remains good, though longer term forecasts are for a surplus to develop," he said.
A world copper surplus of 90,000-100,000 short tons is seen likely in 1996, the Copper Journal's John Gross said Tuesday.
Combined COMEX and LME warehouse stocks show signs of stabilizing though, analysts said.
Combined exchange stocks rose 4,375 tonnes to 295,328 tonnes as of August 30 from 290,953 tonnes on August 23, before slipping back in the past week.
